title: Known-source oracle, negative controls and blinded perceptual trial
summary: A 4-arm experiment retains individual source A, a notch-filtered A, an ordinary A+B overlap, and a deliberate A-even/B-odd weave. Oracle projection requires exact reference A and B and must not be applied as if those references exist for an unknown field clip.
invariants: Two exact and independent source reference PCMs are required by the oracle, with matching alignment, rate and channel geometry.
Least-squares coefficients on two parity groups describe only fit to provided known templates, not human speaker number or source provenance.
A normal overlap, an engineered interleave, and a filtered single source all undergo the identical listening-view pipeline.
Clip identifiers must not encode condition names; the unblinding key is stored separately with restricted permissions and is never published.
Free transcription and confidence are collected before targeted phrases or condition labels are revealed.
A synthetic positive cannot prove field manipulation; sensitivity, specificity, codec, hearing, language and device effects need independent testing.
procedure: Prepare two independently sourced consented voice exemplars, aligned in sample/time without chopping words.
Produce the 4 controlled conditions; keep a hashed, private mapping from anonymous trial codes to conditions.
Level-match gross RMS with headroom, log peak limiting, present anonymous clips and record unprompted transcriptions.
After locking responses, unblind and compare exact-source oracle projection, null confusion and inter-listener disagreement.
Repeat with natural captured overlapping voices, loudspeaker/room playback, noise, codec and unknown-source hold-out data.

provenance.claim: Executable method reference with synthetic tests; no source/media attribution.
